During the winter M&V operating periods (1) and (5), Space_load and Misc_load include both heat gains and losses, as evidenced by the presence of both Space_load_loss/gain and Misc_load_loss/gain values in Table 7. The losses are a result of the infiltration rate and envelope heat loss as well as colder outside air in winter times. Nevertheless, we can see that the net values of these metrics (Space_load and Misc_load) are negative, which makes sense for the winter conditions. The positive value of Misc_load in the CAV HEDS operating mode may be the result of an error in the determination of the enthalpy, due to the low dewpoint sensor accuracy. Enthalpy of mixed, outside and return air streams 2.2.2 Key Observations of Performance Among the 5 M&V Operating Periods • The HEDS HVAC optimization system creates a significant shift in the HVAC system’s behavior in period (2) vs. period (1) when HEDS unit is running based on dewpoint setpoint, even though both periods are being operated in the VAV with HEDS mode of operation. The optimized transition out of the dehumidification mode (period 1) into the cooling mode (period 2) eliminates the need for dewpoint control for the cooling coil. This allows the cooling coil and unit supply air temperatures to be increased, reducing, and even eliminating, the need for the chiller to operate. This change in operation was due to changing weather conditions identified by the logic contained in the HEDS HVAC optimization code while operating in an automatic optimization mode. When the mixed air dewpoint remained below 50 °F and ambient, return air and space conditions allowed, the HEDS optimization code switched to mode 8 – cooling without dehumidification. It remained in this state during the HEDS operation throughout the remainder of the evaluation period. •
